summary: Intune dynamic-group propagation race causes Autopilot provisioning stall and Windows Hello for Business cert enrollment failure
description:
Issue summary: Several new hires' Windows workstations are failing to finish Autopilot provisioning. Devices reach the 'Applying device configuration' stage then hang for 30+ minutes and eventually time out. The common failure downstream is Windows Hello for Business certificate enrollment failing with '0x80092004' (CRYPTO_E_NOT_FOUND) in the local cert store.

Impact: Affected users cannot complete workstation setup; blocking new-hire productivity. Approximately 12 devices observed in the last 48 hours in us-west-2; appears intermittent but reproducible under specific timing.

Environment: Production Autopilot + Intune-managed provisioning. Devices are corporate-provisioned, hybrid Azure AD joined through our provisioning service. BitLocker + WHfB enrollment enabled by default configuration profile.
steps_to_reproduce: Register device with Autopilot and assign to dynamic group 'Corp-Autopilot-ENROLL'
Trigger autopilot provisioning (OOBE) on a new HP ZBook G9 scoped to the group
Observe Intune policy application ordering: Compliance/Configuration profiles, then WHfB cert enrollment profile
If device shows delayed dynamic group membership (Intune backend propagation > 90s), provisioning stalls at 'Applying device configuration'
Wait and observe Windows Hello for Business cert enrollment error in event logs and provisioning timeout
observed_behavior: Provisioning stall at 'Applying device configuration' for 20-40 minutes
EventViewer: Microsoft-Windows-User Device Registration/Admin shows 'WUAUSERV: device registration succeeded' but CertEnroll events show 0x80092004
Intune device pane shows configuration profiles in 'Pending' state until manual refresh or background sync completes
Manual 'Sync' in Company Portal or a targeted policy assignment resolves the device in ~2-5 minutes
expected_behavior: Autopilot provisioning completes within 10 minutes with all assigned profiles applied in correct order
Windows Hello for Business certificate enrollment completes without cryptographic errors
logs: [2026-03-09T14:12:37Z] IntuneService: policyAssignmentPush - payload queued for deviceId=XXX-YYY-001
[2026-03-09T14:12:40Z] IntuneBackend: dynamicGroupResolution - group=Corp-Autopilot-ENROLL lookup returned empty (propagation lag 120s)
[2026-03-09T14:15:05Z] DeviceEvent: CertEnroll failed with hr=0x80092004 (CRYPTO_E_NOT_FOUND) during WHfB cert request
[2026-03-09T14:17:12Z] UserAction: manual sync from Company Portal initiated by support -> subsequent policy apply succeeded
investigation_notes: 03/10: Reproduced in lab by intentionally delaying group membership propagation; provisioning stall correlates with >60s propagation lag in AAD/Intune sync window.

03/11: Intune team confirmed that dynamic group membership is evaluated at the initial registration checkpoint; if group resolution is delayed the device remains in 'pending' state and cert enrollment attempt occurs before required cert template assignment is present.
03/12: Observed race where CertEnroll runs before the machine object receives the 'WHfB-Cert-Profile' assignment -> cert template isn't available locally, leading to 0x80092004 errors.
03/13: Temporary mitigation (manual sync) is effective; long-term fix requires retry logic or reordering of enrollment steps in our provisioning-service or update to Intune sync TTL/push behavior.
Related: INT-50321 has similar symptoms when device inventory de-dupe delayed; referenced for correlation of propagation timing thresholds.

root_cause_hypothesis: Race condition between Intune/AAD dynamic group propagation and provisioning-service's sequence of applying certificates -> cert enrollment begins before assignment exists.
Intune backend can return 'empty' membership on first query due to eventual consistency; no retry performed by provisioning-service.
WHfB certificate enrollment fails with cryptographic error because the cert template/provider is not yet bound to the machine context when CertEnroll is invoked.
temporary_workaround: If provisioning stalls for >8 minutes, instruct L1 to trigger an MDM 'Sync' from Company Portal or run 'dsregcmd /status' then trigger sync via Intune management extension. For onboarding automation, a scheduled background job will perform a retryed sync for devices in 'Applying device configuration' state.
resolution: Workaround implemented: updated runbook for L1 to trigger MDM sync at 8-minute threshold and created automation to attempt up to 3 background syncs. Engineering action: provisioning-service PR#342 adds pre-cert-enroll check (verify WHfB-Cert-Profile assigned) and exponential backoff retries. Plan: deploy PR to staging on 2026-03-16, monitor for 72 hours, then roll to prod. Follow-ups: coordinate with Intune SME to raise MSFT support case if propagation issues persist beyond retries.
